subject: Confidence Interval does not match the p-value in Bootstrapping

messages.author: 7f3e1416cb468ecb
messages.subject: Confidence Interval does not match the p-value in Bootstrapping
parts:
Hello,

I am a bit confused on how to interpret the result we got from the bootstrapping confidence intervals of the mediation effect. As you can see in the table below, the confidence interval does not include zero, and thus it should be interpreted as significant effect. Yet, the p-value clearly indicates a non-significant effect!

> out <-parameterEstimates(fit, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple",level = 0.95, standardized = TRUE);
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Mediation                 estimation   S.Err   stand.value   CI.Lower   CI.Upper   p-value             
Total_ADH_Effect         -0.033   0.018        -0.031     -0.085       -0.008        0.065                  

I read from other posts, that this is a sign of asymmetric confidence interval. If this is the case, how can I be sure? And how to interpret the result and report it in the article? Is it significant or not?


Best regards,
Tahani

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Confidence Interval does not match the p-value in Bootstrapping
parts: Is it significant or not?

What is significance anyway?  The p value is based on assuming a normal sampling distribution.  If it leads to a different conclusion than the bootstrap CI because the bootstrap distribution is not normal, then you should not trust the p value that makes that assumption.  The CI makes no such assumption, so it can be trusted whether the sampling distribution is normal or not.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
